title: A Pilocytic Astrocytoma Mimicking a Clinoidal Meningioma
case_prompt: An 18-year-old woman at 36 weeks’ gestation presented with progressive right-sided visual impairment over several years. Examination revealed right optic nerve pallor and atrophy without other neurologic deficits. A noncontrast brain MRI showed a right supraclinoid mass measuring 2.5 × 2.2 × 2.5 cm. Following delivery, a contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrated an extra-axial mass in the right clinoidal region measuring 2.9 × 3.0 × 2.0 cm, with homogeneous enhancement, a dural tail, encasement of the right internal carotid artery, mild mass effect on the right aspect of the optic chiasm, and possible extension into the right cavernous sinus.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Meningioma was the leading diagnosis because of its radiographic appearance — “Collectively, these findings radiologically suggested a diagnosis of a right clinoidal meningioma.”  
2. Lack of optic nerve infiltration on imaging argued against an optic pathway glioma — “preoperative imaging did not suggest optic nerve infiltration.”  
3. Absence of clinical features of neurofibromatosis type 1 made an optic pathway astrocytoma less likely — “Clinically, our patient had no features of NF1 to support a tumor originating from the optic nerve.”  
4. Accelerated growth during pregnancy supported a hormonally responsive meningioma — “The accelerated interval growth of her lesion during pregnancy was consistent with known effects of gestational hormones on meningioma proliferation.”  
5. Intraoperative finding of optic nerve invasion was unexpected for a meningioma — “further opening of the dura revealed tumor infiltration of the optic nerve, which was unexpected for a meningioma.”  
6. A pilomyxoid astrocytoma variant was considered but imaging lacked its characteristic T2 extension — “Unlike pilocytic astrocytomas, they exhibit T2 signal extension into surrounding deep white and grey matter, in contrast to our patient's radiographic presentation.”
